summary: The candidate correctly adds eager single-host-thread stream ordering and passes its focused tests plus an independent gfx950 event-ordering probe. It is only a partial fix: concurrent CUDA graph replays bypass the host guard, and concurrent host threads can race its unlocked state. Because the candidate also omits a device-side deadline, those same-communicator entry paths can retain the original silent permanent spin rather than complete or fail in a bounded way.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before mechanism check: candidate regression cannot collect because SingleStreamGuard is absent from the exact recorded base. This is not claimed as reproduction of the two-GPU deadlock.
Candidate regression passed 5 tests covering stream change, same-stream fast path, capture skip, and both communicator hooks.
Nine focused and adjacent capability tests passed.

On the assigned gfx950, an eager launch on a second stream was event-ordered after the first; numeric result 2 matched CPU reference 2 and an event was created. This did not execute custom all-reduce.
Independent boundary case confirmed capture is intentionally omitted from guard state: captured work followed by another stream had no event record or wait, leaving concurrent graph replay unordered.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 executed a two-stream host-event ordering probe. No custom all-reduce kernel or multi-GPU collective executed.

remaining_counterexamples: Two CUDA graphs that contain all-reduces from the same communicator can be replayed concurrently on different streams; replay makes no host guard call, so the original shared rendezvous aliasing and unbounded spin remain possible.

Two host threads can concurrently issue on different streams and race the guard's unlocked per-communicator state; the omitted device deadline means a resulting protocol collision can still hang permanently.
The legacy AOT implementation retains an unbounded device spin as well; the eager host guard narrows exposure but does not provide bounded failure for bypasses or races.
remaining_limitations: The environment had one AMD gfx950 GPU, not the two NVIDIA A100 NVLink GPUs required for the reported reproduction.
CUDA CustomAllReduceV2, green contexts, two-rank execution, full model serving, and multi-node behavior were not run.
The candidate changed no native source, so no native rebuild was applicable; no CUDA compiler or ISA evidence could be collected in this ROCm-only environment.
The base failure evidence verifies absence of the guard, not the original hardware deadlock.
